CONCLUSION AND FUTURE WORK Thisprojectfocusedondevelopingacommon-modesolid-statetransformer(CM-SST)tomitigate the effects of the E3 component of high-altitude electromagnetic pulse (HEMP) and geomagnetic disturbance(GMD)events. Theeffortsuccessfullydeliveredresultsinthreekeyareas: • Architecture Development: A hardware architecture was designed to generate controlled common-mode (CM) voltages without disturbing AC power or voltage. A hardware pro- totype, based on this architecture, was built and validated against simulation models. This prototype also served as a reference platform for other RES Mission Campaign LDRDs, in- cludinga projectled byTylerBowman thatexamines thesusceptibilityof SSTarchitectures tothefasterE1andE2componentsofaHEMPevent. • Control Design: Nonlinear control strategies based on Hamiltonian Surface Shaping and Power Flow (HSSPF) methods were developed and implemented to maintain stability and accurately track current setpoints during CM disturbances. Hardware testing confirmed the controller’s ability to suppress CM-induced current offsets and protect inverter switches during simulated disturbances. The control models and findings have been shared with a system-levelcontrolsprojectunderDavidWilsonforintegrationandjointanalysis. • System-Level Simulation Studies: Reduced-order modeling and large-scale simulation studiesdemonstratedthatfullgridprotectioncanbeachievedwithoutreplacingeverytrans- former. In many scenarios, replacing or modifying only about half of the transformers to hybridSSTs(H-SSTs)providedsufficientmitigationofCMdisturbances. Thesestudiesalso establishedstrategiesforoptimalplacementofCM-SSTandH-SSTunits,whichwillinform futuredesignsanddeploymentstrategies. Looking forward, the primary need is to scale the hardware to grid-relevant voltages and power levels. This will be addressed in a related LDRD project, ‘Grid-Ready Hybrid Solid State Trans- formersforEnhancedGridResilience’,beginninginFY26. Thiseffortwillfocusondevelopingan H-SSTarchitecturethatintegratestheCM-SSTwithaconventionaltransformer. Inthisconfigura- tion,theconventionaltransformerprovidesvoltagestep-down,whilethepowerelectronicsoperate entirely on the low-voltage side, reducing the need for high-voltage blocking devices or complex module stacking. This new project will also extend system-level simulation and optimization ef- fortstomodelswithmorethan100buses,benchmarkingthehybridSSTarchitectureagainstother proposed HEMP mitigation strategies.
